note: Every slot below has a synthesised fallback, so the game is complete with no files. To use a recorded sound, drop the file in this folder and put its filename in "file". gain / offset / maxSeconds are the mix details measured from the recording: gain lifts a quiet file, offset skips the dead air before the sound starts, maxSeconds cuts a long tail with a short fade.

shuffle.when: The deck is riffled before every deal
shuffle.style: A real riffle: cards cascade for about 1.4 s, then the pack is squared and tapped twice on the felt. The shuffle animation is timed to this file.

deal.when: Each card leaves the deck into a hand (played in a run)
deal.style: A short, dry card slide. It is played dozens of times in a row, so it is held back in the mix.

flip.when: A card turns from face-down to face-up
flip.style: A tiny snap of card stock. Quieter than deal.

place.when: A card lands on the trick tray
place.style: Card on felt, with a soft low body. The most repeated sound in the game, so it sits just under the events.

select.when: Tapping a card, a trump suit, a settings control
select.style: A soft wooden tick, not a digital click.

invalid.when: Trying to play a card you are not allowed to play
invalid.style: A gentle two-note nudge down. Never a buzzer.

trickWin.style: A warm rising chime over the cards. Frequent, so the tail is trimmed to keep it from smearing.

trickLose.style: The same family as trickWin but settling downward. Quiet - the player loses often.

trump.style: A short bright flourish, like a card being turned over with intent.

coin.when: The coin is tossed and spins in the air
coin.style: Metallic ring plus air, long enough to cover the whole flight.

coinLand.when: The coin lands and the toss result is shown
coinLand.style: A coin bouncing on the table, brighter than a card. The recording has 0.7 s of silence first; offset starts at the clink.

matchPoint.when: Either player reaches one point from the match win
matchPoint.style: A rising two-note bell with a soft shimmer over a low body: "almost there", without celebrating yet. Generated from the game's own synth by tests/render-sound.js, so this file and the synth fallback are the same cue. Replace it with a recording and the slot keeps working.

victory.style: A short warm fanfare. The recording is quiet and has a long silent tail; gain lifts it and maxSeconds trims the tail.

defeat.style: A graceful three-note descent. Sympathetic, never mocking. The supplied recording is 0.36 s, so the whole file is the cue; there is no tail to trim.
